questions.prompt: Marion books her holiday in April. She pays 200 dinars at the counter that day and the rest of what she owes a month before she flies. What are the 200 dinars called?

options.text: a refund
a discount
a deposit
a voucher

questions.explanation: What you hand over on the day you book, so that the agency holds the place for you, is a deposit; what remains of the price follows later and is called the balance. A refund travels the other way — the agency gives you back money you had already handed over. A discount moves no money at all: it only makes a bill you have not yet settled smaller. And a voucher is not money either: it is the slip you present at the desk for something that has already been bought.

questions.prompt: A guest tells the hotel manager: "The room was not exactly the one your brochure shows." How should he understand her?

options.text: she is praising the room and the brochure that describes it
she is making a complaint about the room, in a quiet voice
she is asking the manager to show her the brochure again
she is saying that she has not yet read the brochure

questions.explanation: English complains by understating: "not exactly the one your brochure shows" is a quiet way of saying that the room and the photograph had nothing in common. The politeness is in the voice, not in the strength of the complaint, and the manager who hears only politeness will be surprised by the letter that follows. Nothing in the sentence praises anything, it asks for no document, and a guest who had never read the brochure could not compare the room with it.

questions.prompt: Marion writes to the agency: "You said that we would be met at the airport ___" Which ending turns her sentence into a complaint?

options.text: and a driver was waiting for us with a sign.
because our flight arrived long after midnight.
so we booked the same package again this year.
but nobody was waiting for us when we landed.

questions.explanation: Reporting a promise is not yet complaining about it: "You said that we would be met at the airport" is a neutral report until something contradicts it. The complaint is born of the contrast, promise on one side and reality on the other, joined by but. A driver actually waiting confirms the promise instead of breaking it; the hour of the flight explains a fact and blames nobody; and booking the same package again says that the customer was satisfied.

questions.prompt: In which of these words does the main stress fall on the SECOND syllable?

options.text: deposit
package
travel
schedule

questions.explanation: Deposit is said de-POS-it: the middle syllable is the loud one, and the two around it drop away. The three others all carry their stress at the front — PACK-age, TRAV-el, SCHED-ule — and that holds whichever way you pronounce the beginning of SCHED-ule. Stress belongs to an English word as firmly as its spelling does, and an agent who is handed a DE-po-sit hears no word he knows.

questions.prompt: The agent sells Marion a package holiday. What does that mean?

options.text: she chooses her hotel once she has landed, not before
she pays for the flight now and for the hotel on arrival
one price covers the flight, the hotel and the transfers
she can cancel the booking at any time and pay nothing

questions.explanation: A package holiday is sold as one product at one price: the flight, the hotel and the transfers between airport and hotel are bought together, which is what makes it cheaper than three separate bookings. Paying the hotel on arrival is what happens when you book the parts separately; choosing the hotel after landing is exactly what a package prevents; and cancelling costs nothing only before the date printed in the booking conditions, after which the deposit is lost.
